name: greenfield-from-intention-map
prompt: Given an intention map for engineers who need to resume recent work, find documents, manage projects, review changes, and see what needs attention, design the information architecture for a small MVP.
must: derive a conceptual/object model before navigation UI
distinguish global, contextual, utility, and any justified cross-cutting destinations
trace primary intentions through the structure
leave screen composition to downstream UX specification

name: existing-messy-app-reconstruct-first
prompt: The app currently has sidebar items Home, Projects, Tasks, Reviews, Documents, Recent, Favorites, Search and Settings, plus project tabs Overview, Tasks, Files, Activity. Improve the navigation.
must: reconstruct the actual conceptual/destination model before proposing new navigation
identify mixed global/contextual ownership and duplicate concepts
preserve coherent existing conventions where possible

name: ambiguous-review-ownership
prompt: We need Reviews. They can belong to a document, a project, and also appear in a user's work queue. Decide where Reviews should live.
must: model the Review object and its relationships/ownership
distinguish object ownership from navigation entry points
explain trade-offs and converge on a recommendation
must_not: assume one sidebar destination solves all contexts

name: action-is-not-destination
prompt: Add Create Task, Export, Open Items, and Settings to the main navigation.
must: classify each requested item as action, status/filter, or destination before placing it
challenge navigation items that are not true destinations

name: negative-trigger-screen-layout
prompt: On the document screen, should the inspector panel be 320px or 360px wide and should comments be tabs or an accordion?
must: recognize this is primarily surface specification rather than cross-surface information architecture
must_not: rewrite the product IA without evidence of a structural issue
